title: Progressive disclosure
summary: Hide secondary or advanced detail until it becomes relevant, while keeping the disclosure control visible, understandable, and reversible.
problem: Showing every option at once increases cognitive load, but hiding important information behind ambiguous controls makes features undiscoverable.
use_when: Secondary detail is useful to some users but not required for the primary task
Advanced options would otherwise dominate the interface
avoid_when: The hidden content contains information needed to make the current decision
Most users need the content immediately
rationale: Progressive disclosure can reduce initial complexity without deleting capability.
The control must communicate that more content exists.

prefer_alternatives_if: The information is short and important enough to show directly
use_if: Secondary detail is useful to some users but not required for the primary task
Advanced options would otherwise dominate the interface

requirements: Do not make hover the only way to reveal content.
keyboard: Enter and Space activate the disclosure control.

requirements: Keep the disclosed content adjacent or clearly related to its trigger.
Preserve user choice while they remain in the task.
